name: Photo renamer
pitch: Renames every photo file with the date it was taken, so the file name matches the capture time.
instructions: Start by listing all files in the person's photo folder. For each file, read its metadata to find the date it was taken. If the file has a date, create a new name using that date in YYYY-MM-DD format, keeping the original file extension. If the file has no date or the date cannot be read, skip it and move to the next file. After processing every file, write a summary list showing which files were renamed and which were skipped. Show this summary to the person so they can review the changes. When nothing is found, say so and list no files.

examples.does: list the photo files and begin checking their dates
show the summary of renamed and skipped files

skills.name: extract-date-from-file
skills.description: Read a file's metadata to find the date it was taken.
skills.body: 1. Use shell_run to run exiftool on the file and capture the output. 2. Look for the line that starts with "Date: " or "Create Date". 3. Extract the date part in YYYY:MM:DD format. 4. If no date line is found, report that the file has no date.

skills.name: rename-file
skills.description: Change a file name using the extracted date.
skills.body: 1. Build the new name by taking the extracted date, replacing the colons with hyphens, and appending the original file extension. 2. Use file_write to rename the file from its old name to the new name. 3. If the new name already exists, add a number in parentheses before the extension to avoid overwriting.

readme:
# Photo renamer
Renames every photo file with the date it was taken, so the file name matches the capture time.

**What it does**
- Lists all files in the photo folder
- Reads each file's date-taken metadata
- Renames files to YYYY-MM-DD filename.ext
- Shows a summary of renamed and skipped files

**What it needs**
- Access to the person's photo folder
- The shell_run tool to read image metadata
- The file_list, file_read and file_write tools to process files

**What it will not do**
- It cannot rename files that have no date metadata
- It will not change file extensions or move files to another folder
